book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 1 — Marley's Ghost
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.role: protagonist — cold, miserly old man who is redeemed
cast.canonical: a bent thin miserly old man with a sharp pointed nose, shrivelled frowning face and thin lips, in a long shabby dark tailcoat, carrying a cane
cast.anchor: a bent thin old man, pointed nose, hard frown, shabby dark tailcoat + cane

cast.name: Marley's Ghost
cast.role: Scrooge's dead partner — a warning spirit
cast.canonical: a translucent ghostly man in an old-fashioned pigtail, waistcoat and tights, a cloth bandage tied round his head and jaw, wound in a long heavy chain made of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks and ledgers
cast.anchor: translucent ghost, head-bandage + pigtail, bound in a chain of cash-boxes and padlocks

cast.name: Bob Cratchit
cast.canonical: a thin poor clerk with a mild kindly face, wrapped in a long white woollen comforter scarf and fingerless mittens, no overcoat
cast.anchor: thin clerk, long white comforter scarf, fingerless mittens, no coat

cast.name: Fred
cast.canonical: a handsome ruddy cheerful young man with side-whiskers and bright eyes, glowing with warmth, a scarf and a sprig of holly on his coat
cast.anchor: ruddy glowing young man, side-whiskers, holly sprig, warm laugh

panels.scene: a bleak snowy London churchyard at dusk, a fresh gravestone reading MARLEY, a bent thin sharp-nosed old man in a long shabby dark tailcoat standing coldly over it with his cane, unmoved
panels.composition: wide, a cold opening at the grave

teen.narration: LONDON, SEVEN YEARS AGO. SCROOGE'S PARTNER MARLEY HAS DIED.

bubbles.text: Marley was dead: to begin with.
Old Marley was as dead as a door-nail.
There is no doubt whatever about that.
There is no doubt that Marley was dead.

panels.scene: a grimy counting-house door beneath a weathered sign reading SCROOGE AND MARLEY, the bent sharp-nosed old man in his shabby tailcoat unlocking it, tight-fisted and sour
panels.composition: close, the miser and his firm

teen.narration: YEARS PASS. SCROOGE KEEPS THE OLD FIRM'S NAME.

bubbles.text: Scrooge never painted out Old Marley's name.
The firm was known as Scrooge and Marley.
he answered to both names. It was all the same to him.
he answered to both names

panels.scene: a tight close portrait of the bent old miser, sharp pointed nose, shrivelled frowning cheek, thin blue lips, red eyes, a frosty rime on his brow, radiating cold
panels.composition: close, the coldest man in London

bubbles.text: a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner!
Hard and sharp as flint... secret, and self-contained, and solitary as an oyster.
he iced his office in the dog-days; and didn't thaw it one degree at Christmas.

panels.scene: the sharp-nosed old miser walking a frozen London street, snow and wind streaming past him while he ignores it entirely, a self-contained aura of cold about him

bubbles.text: The cold within him froze his old features, nipped his pointed nose, shrivelled his cheek
No warmth could warm, no wintry weather chill him.
Foul weather didn't know where to have him.

panels.scene: the dim counting-house on Christmas Eve, the sharp-nosed miser at a big ledger by a tiny fire, and beyond a thin clerk in a long white comforter scarf shivering over letters at a single coal, fog at the window

teen.narration: CHRISTMAS EVE. SCROOGE WORKS HIS CLERK, BOB CRATCHIT, IN THE COLD.

bubbles.text: It was cold, bleak, biting weather: foggy withal
the clerk's fire was so very much smaller that it looked like one coal
The fog came pouring in at every chink and keyhole

panels.scene: a ruddy glowing cheerful young man with side-whiskers and a holly sprig bursting in from the frosty street, arms wide, while the sour sharp-nosed miser scowls over his ledger

teen.narration: HIS NEPHEW FRED ARRIVES, GLOWING WITH CHRISTMAS.

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: A merry Christmas, uncle! God save you!

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Bah!... Humbug!
his face was ruddy and handsome; his eyes sparkled, and his breath smoked again.

panels.scene: the sour miser and the ruddy cheerful nephew arguing across the counting-house desk, the old man jabbing a bony finger, the young man open-handed and warm

teen.narration: THEY SPAR OVER THE MEANING OF CHRISTMAS.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: What right have you to be merry? What reason have you to be merry? You're poor enough.

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: What right have you to be dismal? What reason have you to be morose? You're rich enough.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: What else can I be... when I live in such a world of fools as this?

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: keep Christmas in your own way, and let me keep it in mine

panels.scene: the ruddy cheerful nephew speaking warmly with shining eyes, hand on his heart, the clerk in the white scarf secretly delighted behind him

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: a kind, forgiving, charitable, pleasant time

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: it has never put a scrap of gold or silver in my pocket... and I say, God bless it!

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: when men and women seem by one consent to open their shut-up hearts freely

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: as if they really were fellow-passengers to the grave

panels.scene: two plump kindly gentlemen with hats off and subscription books bowing to the scowling sharp-nosed miser at his desk, asking for charity

teen.narration: TWO GENTLEMEN COME COLLECTING FOR THE POOR.

bubbles.speaker: GENTLEMAN
bubbles.text: make some slight provision for the Poor and destitute, who suffer greatly at the present time

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Are there no prisons?

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: And the Union workhouses?... Are they still in operation?

panels.scene: the cold miser waving the charity gentlemen away with a hard sneer, turning back to his money, utterly without pity

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: If they would rather die... they had better do it, and decrease the surplus population.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: It's not my business

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: It's enough for a man to understand his own business, and not to interfere with other people's.

panels.scene: night, the thin clerk in his long white comforter scarf gleefully sliding down an icy lane behind a line of boys under the gas-lamps, free for Christmas, while the miser stalks off alone

teen.narration: SCROOGE GRUDGINGLY GIVES BOB CHRISTMAS DAY OFF.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: A poor excuse for picking a man's pocket every twenty-fifth of December!
went down a slide on Cornhill... in honour of its being Christmas Eve
ran home to Camden Town as hard as he could pelt, to play at blindman's-buff.

panels.scene: the sharp-nosed miser recoiling at his own front door as the heavy brass door-knocker has become the ghostly glowing face of Marley, spectacles pushed up on its spectral forehead, a dismal light around it
panels.composition: close, the knocker becomes a face

teen.narration: AT HOME THAT NIGHT, THE DOOR-KNOCKER CHANGES.

bubbles.text: not a knocker, but Marley's face.
with ghostly spectacles turned up on its ghostly forehead
It was not angry or ferocious, but looked at Scrooge as Marley used to look
As Scrooge looked fixedly at this phenomenon, it was a knocker again.

panels.scene: the miser in nightcap and dressing-gown starting up from his chair by a low fire as a disused bell high on the wall swings wildly of its own accord, dread on his face

teen.narration: ALONE BY THE FIRE, A DEAD BELL BEGINS TO RING.

bubbles.text: he saw this bell begin to swing
soon it rang out loudly, and so did every bell in the house.
It was with great astonishment, and with a strange, inexplicable dread
It swung so softly in the outset that it scarcely made a sound

panels.scene: the terrified miser clutching his chair as a heavy clanking of dragged chains rises up a dark stairwell toward his door, a booming cellar door thrown open below

teen.narration: THEN — DRAGGING CHAINS, CLIMBING TOWARD HIM.

bubbles.text: The cellar-door flew open with a booming sound
then coming up the stairs; then coming straight towards his door.
ghosts in haunted houses were described as dragging chains

panels.scene: the translucent ghost of Marley in pigtail and waistcoat passing through the closed door, wound in a long heavy chain forged of cash-boxes, padlocks, keys and ledgers, a cloth bandage tied round its head, the miser cowering

teen.narration: MARLEY'S GHOST ENTERS — BOUND IN A DREADFUL CHAIN.

bubbles.text: made... of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers, deeds, and heavy purses
His body was transparent
the chilling influence of its death-cold eyes
looking through his waistcoat, could see the two buttons on his coat behind

panels.scene: the miser in nightcap trying to sneer at the spectral bound ghost seated across the low fire, half-terrified, cracking a nervous joke

teen.narration: SCROOGE TRIES TO DENY HIS OWN EYES.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: You may be an undigested bit of beef, a blot of mustard, a crumb of cheese

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: There's more of gravy than of grave about you, whatever you are!
You may be an undigested bit of beef

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: A slight disorder of the stomach makes them cheats.

panels.scene: the anguished translucent ghost lifting its heavy chain of cash-boxes at arm's length, wringing its shadowy hands, the miser on his knees before it

teen.narration: MARLEY REVEALS THE CHAIN HE MADE IN LIFE.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: I wear the chain I forged in life... I made it link by link, and yard by yard

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: Mankind was my business.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: charity, mercy, forbearance, and benevolence, were, all, my business.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: The dealings of my trade were but a drop of water in the comprehensive ocean of my business!

panels.scene: the translucent ghost floating backward out of the wide-open window into a night sky filled with chained wailing phantoms, one last warning gesture to the kneeling miser
panels.composition: wide, the warning and the phantom night

teen.narration: MARLEY GIVES HIS WARNING AND JOINS THE PHANTOMS OF THE NIGHT.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: You will be haunted... by Three Spirits.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: Expect the first to-morrow, when the bell tolls One.
The air was filled with phantoms, wandering hither and thither in restless haste

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: you have yet a chance and hope of escaping my fate
